The pessimism lives in the UNCALIBRATED valuation layer that sits on top of the statements, and it decomposes cleanly: (i) the r2 sliding schedule and terminal normalisation the house already wrote and never enforced (PHDC DCF 14.86 -> 27.83, central -> 16.78, +10% vs price; TMGH capacity 53.05 -> 74.38 with an inflation-coherent terminal growth); (ii) a four-lens weighted average that blends the DCF with two Fisher-incoherent floors (96% of PHDC's published gap, 100% of AMOC's, 71% of ARCC's); (iii) specification and bridge defects the gap reviews already priced and left in the code (TMGH 53.05 -> 89.47 at the unchanged rate); (iv) an ERP basis chosen per study against the protocol's own 'CDS PRIMARY' line (worth +8% PHDC, +12.5% TMGH); (v) a terminal reinvestment mechanic that double-charges inflation (ARCC central 54.10 -> 66.92). Applied together, with the CONSERVATIVE reading of each and no price input, TMGH's capacity case prints 96.45 (-1.4%) and PHDC 16.78 (+10%) — the whole named gap is method incoherence. On the DCF lens alone, three of five names (AMOC +7.4%, ARCC -2.4%, PHDC -2.2%) were already within 8% of price at house rates; the statements are not where the money is. That said, the principal's instinct that 'the calibration process is wrong' is correct in two specific, fixable ways that are NOT the ones stated: first, the walk-forward grades only drivers, so a study can pass it with a perfect income statement and a fair value 60% off — the missing instrument is a VALUATION-LAYER walk-forward (log(FV_t / P_{t+h}) at 7-13 historical origins per name on point-in-time drivers, rates and macro; explicitly permitted under [R-LENS-01] as a grade; buildable now for 31 of 37 EG names with >=10 year-end closes), with pre-registered candidate constructions (glide vs flat, CDS vs rating, DCF-only vs blend, E/(Ke-pi) vs E/Ke, minority at value share) selected ONLY by that out-of-sample grade so the promotion rule is honoured and price never enters a study; second, where the statement walk-forward does find pessimism (revenue under-forecast on 4 of 5, sign-robust) its correction bar converts it to watch flags and the studies then build below their own records (TMGH -23.5% on FY2026 revenue) — the remedy there is to fix the specification the records themselves blame (recognition clock, interest base, macro path) rather than to lower the correction bar, and to make a gap-review finding either land in the code in the same commit or be declined with a reason. The four gates that would have stopped every item above are mechanical and cheap: assert the r2 glide (WACC_TERM < WACC_EXP, terminal ERP normalised) on every Egyptian study; assert Fisher coherence (every nominal g, escalator and lens capitalisation rate registered against one house inflation path, real growth stated); assert a single ERP basis and a single dated rf per market per build; assert the bridge (minority at a stated value basis with all three framings printed, every balance-sheet line classified). None exists today, which is why a process that was individually right at every step was collectively blind at the output.

Each cause's share is the fraction of a name's EGP/share gap that the counterfactual closes, computed by re-running the study's OWN committed code (engine/phdc_study/valuation_v2.py, engine/tmgh_study/valuation.py + model.py, reproducing the published 14.8642 and 53.0455 first) or read from the study's own gap_review_calcs.json / study_numbers.json sensitivity grids. EGCH is analysed and then set aside: its gap is a conclusion about a capital programme, not an instance of the house lean. The layers are: STATEMENT (drivers, macro path — what [R-FCAL-01] scores), VALUATION (cost of capital, terminal, lens blend, bridge — what nothing scores), PROCESS (which framing gets adopted when two exist, which gates exist, which direction they fire).
verdict: Yes, the house is systematically pessimistic on Egypt, and the pessimism lives almost entirely in the uncalibrated valuation layer, not in the statement projections: on the three names that blend lenses the DCF lens itself sits within +7.4% / −2.4% / −2.2% of the price (AMOC 9.77 vs 9.10, ARCC 57.60 vs 59.00, PHDC 14.86 vs 15.20) and the published discounts of −5%, −8% and −28% are manufactured by three floor lenses at typed weights (PHDC: −3.92 of the −4.26/sh gap, 92%; AMOC: DCF-only flips the sign; ARCC: 71%). On the two names the principal named the largest single lever is the house breaking its own r2 rule — PHDC and TMGH discount every year and the perpetuity at a flat crisis WACC (26.25% / 35.79%) with no glide and Egypt's Caa1 premium held for ever, which the protocol (Standing_Research_Protocol.md:304-348) forbids for every new Egyptian study and which its own measurement says understates an Egyptian DCF by ~162% (SRP:493, RMDA), and no gate checks: applying the AMOC/ARCC glide through PHDC's own code moves its DCF 14.86→27.83 and its central 10.94→16.78 (+10% vs 15.20), and TMGH's capacity case 53.05→74-90 (48-82% of the gap). The collapse of PHDC (15.89→10.94) and TMGH (147.12→39.33) was the 18%→26.25%/35.79% cost-of-capital step (fv_movement.json, Driver Ledger: 'essentially all of it is the cost of capital'), not the walk-forward, which changed exactly one number in ~170 scored cells (ARCC depreciation ×1.0298) and whose TMGH corrections carry 0.000 log with an emptied corrections_log.json. Underneath sits a Ke construction no EGX investor uses — a stripped local yield plus β×13.94% charges Egypt's default risk 1.52β times net (1.4× on AMOC, 2.2× on TMGH), gives nominal Ke of 27-37% (real 11-19%) against an EGX30 that returned 17.0%/21.9% nominal over 15y/10y, and against a market that prices TMGH at rf*+β×4.6% (mature ERP, zero country premium) — while the cleaner names' price-implied Ke cluster at 26-31% says the defensible correction is a term structure and a few points, not 8-14pp. The rest is process: a one-sided gap gate whose stated counterweight ('the walk-forward finds this house optimistic') is contradicted by scores.json on four of five names, six quantified corrections found by the gap reviews and shipped unapplied, and a habit of adopting the more punitive framing wherever two exist (minority, ERP basis, provisions).

The revenue/cost driver models on AMOC, ARCC and PHDC. Their DCF lenses sit at +7.4% / −2.4% / −2.2% of price at the house's own flat or glided rates; the published discounts on those names are lens blend, bridge and beta, not the statements. (TMGH's driver model IS a cause — RC-4/RC-6 — but as a specification choice made against its own record, not as a calibration failure.)

EGCH's 73% discount. It is a conclusion about the ANNA programme (EGP 14.7bn unspent, modelled at zero EBIT after depreciation at 50% utilisation / USD 280/t): price-implied flat rate 7.9% (study_numbers drivers.implied_wacc_base), no cell of the USD 380-540 × 17-24% grid exceeds 3.67/sh, and even a flat 15% rate only reaches 1.18. Terminal-ERP normalisation adds ~0.9-1.5/sh and the statutory-tax construction +0.44 on the central; the rest is a legitimate contrarian call and must not be folded into the 'house lean'. (Its 17%-real terminal Ke is an instance of RC-3, but it does not explain EGCH.)
The rf* normalisation (rf − sovereign default spread). It LOWERS Ke by 3.4-6.4pp; it is the correct removal of the v1 double-count. The problem is what is added back through β (RC-3), not the strip.

Cash charged twice / negative debt weights. Fixed on AMOC on 01-Sep (31.19%→27.45%); cash is now mechanically charged once on all five (no finance income in any FCFF, cash or net debt added once). The AMOC prose still asserts the retired theory; the code does not.

The five-year explicit horizon. Extending PHDC to ten years at its trailing 25.2% CPI gives 35.62 (an extrapolation, not a forecast); at coherent inflation it gives 11.65 on the flat rate — the horizon is not the lever, the rates being extended are.

The stale 23.00% ten-year quote against a 19.00% policy rate, and the three different Egyptian rf values across the five studies (22.31 / 22.95 / 23.00%). Worth ±1pp of Ke, ±0.6-0.9pp of WACC; real but minor; it is a symptom of the missing Cost_of_Capital_Reference.md, not a cause of a 28-60% gap.

The process gates that exist (Step 0.0, SIGCM, assert_beta_provenance, assert_ground_up, check_workbook_structure, recalculation, scrub, table/figure discipline). The MC price engine, the technical read and the three-lens independence rule [R-LENS-01]. They do not enter fair value. [R-LENS-01] also does NOT forbid the fix: it permits price to GRADE a method ('the value-gap IC may be measured forever as a diagnostic'), only forbidding price as an INPUT — so a valuation-layer walk-forward is sanctioned and is the missing instrument.

'The market must be right'. is_the_statement_calibration_the_problem: No — and it is also not a working calibration, which is why the principal's expectation cannot be met by it. Direct answer in three parts. (1) It is not the SOURCE of the pessimism: across five names and ~170 scored cells the walk-forward changed one number in one valuation (ARCC depreciation ×1.0298); TMGH's four 'adopted' corrections carry 0.000 log into the forward path and its committed corrections_log.json is empty; the edition movements the principal saw (PHDC 15.89→10.94, TMGH 147.12→39.33) were the 18%→26.25%/35.79% cost-of-capital step applied FLAT into perpetuity against the house's own r2 rule (RC-1), plus a minority-at-book deduction and a −26%-real sales fade (RC-4) — none of which the walk-forward touched or can see. (2) It is not the RIGHT INSTRUMENT for the question asked: [R-FCAL-01] grades statement drivers against later statements; on the three blending names the DCF lens built from those drivers is already within +7.4/−2.4/−2.2% of price, and the published gaps are produced downstream by the discount-rate path and level (RC-1, RC-3), the lens blend (RC-2), the bridge (RC-4) and beta (RC-8) — a layer that no test in the repository grades against anything, while the only value-vs-price measurement (value_gap_backtest, n=32, IC −0.14, INSUFFICIENT-POWER) is a one-date cross-section. Calibrating the statements harder will not move fair value toward price by construction. (3) It is nonetheless BROKEN in its own terms, in the pessimistic direction: it measures the method under-forecasting revenue on four of five names (AMOC −0.57, ARCC −0.28, EGCH −0.60, TMGH new sales −0.88 log; profit loses to 'freeze' at one year on four of five) and its pre-registered rules turn every one of those biases into a watch flag acted on by nobody; the studies then build BELOW the record (TMGH FY2026 revenue −23.5%, new sales −38.6% vs its own walk-forward central); the digest cites 'the walk-forward's finding that this house leans optimistic' as the counterweight to a one-sided gate when the finding rests on PHDC alone and is a recognition-clock specification error. What is needed is not a better statement calibration but a VALUATION-LAYER walk-forward, which [R-LENS-01] explicitly permits (price grades, never inputs): origins at each fiscal year-end with ≥5 years of statements (PHDC/TMGH FY2015-24, EGCH FY2012-24, ARCC FY2018-24; AMOC skip), point-in-time Ke rebuilt from that year's sovereign yield, Damodaran vintage and a beta regressed to the origin, the house terminal and lens rules as of that origin, scored as log(FV_t/P_{t+h}) for h = 1-3 against FV = P_t and own-median-multiple naive benchmarks, with a lever decomposition (drivers at realised statements, Ke construction variants, terminal path, blend vs DCF-only, bridge) — candidates pre-registered from external principles and only SELECTED by the out-of-sample grade so the PROMOTION RULE holds. Until that exists, the four fixes the house's own documents already prescribe close most of the gap without any price input: enforce the r2 glide and terminal normalisation on PHDC/TMGH (PHDC central 10.94→16.78; TMGH capacity 53.05→74-90), apply the gap-review corrections already computed (TMGH 53.05→89.47 at the unchanged rate; PHDC +0.5-3.9/sh), make the DCF/class lens the central with the floor lenses re-specified under Fisher and shown as cross-checks (AMOC +7.4%, ARCC −2.4%, PHDC −2.2%), and adopt one ERP basis with the CRP charged once (2-5pp of Ke on the far-below names). Four of five would then sit inside ±10% of price; EGCH would not, and should not be forced to.

framing: Unit of analysis: the signed gap ln(central/spot) per name, struck on the studies' own committed numbers (AMOC 8.64/9.10 = −0.052; ARCC 54.10/59.00 = −0.087; PHDC 10.94/15.20 = −0.329; TMGH capacity 53.05/97.80 = −0.612, four-case median 39.33 = −0.911; EGCH 3.76/13.98 = −1.313). A cause's share is the fraction of that gap closed when ONE lever is moved to the construction the house's own written rules or its own gap review prescribe, holding everything else at published — computed by re-running the study's own code (engine/phdc_study/valuation_v2.py, engine/tmgh_study/valuation.py + model.py) or read from its committed grids (engine/arcc_study/study_numbers.json sensitivity, engine/amoc_study/study_numbers.json sens). Shares can exceed 100% and overlap: on PHDC the term-structure lever and the lens-blend lever EACH close the whole gap, so both cannot be applied without overshooting; where levers are multiplicative (TMGH rate × minority × fade) I state the joint result rather than sum the parts. Movement between editions is read from engine/fv_movement.json and the studies' derived.prior_edition fields. Nothing below uses the price as an input to any construction; it is used only to grade, which [R-LENS-01] permits ('the value-gap IC may be measured forever as a diagnostic'). Two reproductions were done before any lever was moved: PHDC dcf(cfo_mid, 0.2625) = 14.8642 and TMGH discounted('capacity', 0.35793)+bridge = 53.0455, both exact. The EGX30 anchors were recomputed from engine/raw_indices/EG/EGX30.csv (15y 16.97%, 10y 21.91%, rolling 10-year CAGR over 1,245 windows: median 12.9%, p90 19.6%, maximum 25.1%). The value-gap backtest (engine/value_gap_backtest_EG_20260824.json) is n=32 at 1M, IC −0.140, p=0.45, 3M n=0 — it cannot adjudicate anything and is not used as evidence in either direction.
verdict: Yes, the house is systematically pessimistic on Egypt, and the size is large on the two names the principal raised: the five-name mean signed gap moved from −12.2% (site values) to −42.0% (rebuilt editions) to −34.9% (after the manual gap reviews), and all five now sit below the price where two sat above. The pessimism does not come from the statement calibration: across ~170 scored cells the [R-FCAL-01] machinery changed exactly one number (ARCC manufacturing depreciation ×1.0298, engine/arcc_study/compute.py:480), TMGH's four 'adopted' corrections carried 0.000 into the projection and its committed corrections_log.json is empty, and the −31% (PHDC) and −73% (TMGH) collapses are entirely the cost-of-capital step from a hardcoded 18% to 26.25%/35.79% (PHDC DCF at 18% = 48.50; TMGH capacity at 18% = 195.38, engine/tmgh_study/study_numbers.json lenses.sensitivity.wacc_grid). It comes from an uncalibrated valuation layer where every binary choice was resolved in the lower direction: a flat crisis-era WACC held through a perpetuity in breach of the protocol's own r2 sliding-schedule rule (worth 100%+ of PHDC's gap and 46–106% of TMGH's capacity gap depending only on glide shape), a four-lens blend whose two nominal-stasis lenses produce 92% of PHDC's and 100%+ of AMOC's gap, a minority deducted at 45% of book against a 21% filed profit share (47% of TMGH's gap), and a −26%-real sales fade the study's own walk-forward said ran the wrong way (60% of TMGH's gap). Applying only rules the house has already written — the SRP r2 glide, the gap reviews' own computed corrections, NEP at ke−g — puts PHDC at 15.7–16.2 (+3 to +7% vs 15.20) and TMGH's capacity case at 89.47 (−8.5%) before any change to the rate level, and AMOC/ARCC are already within 3–8% on their DCF lens alone. EGCH (−73%) is the one genuine disagreement with the market that no discount rate closes (implied flat rate 7.9%), and even there the walk-forward measured a 55-of-55-cell revenue under-forecast of −0.60 log that the correction rule refused to act on.

root_causes.cause: The discount rate's TERM STRUCTURE: PHDC and TMGH discount every explicit year, a 14-year residual annuity and the perpetuity at a single flat crisis-era WACC (26.25%, 35.79%) built on a 23.00% ten-year yield quoted at the top of a cutting cycle (policy rate 19.00%), and EGCH/PHDC/TMGH carry Damodaran's Caa1 country premium (9.71 of the 13.94% ERP) into perpetuity — in direct breach of the house's own binding 13-Jul r2 procedure, which no gate enforces.
root_causes.layer: VALUATION — cost of capital (term structure and terminal), not the statement projection
root_causes.mechanism: A perpetuity capitalised at a rate that embeds 14–16% inflation and a crisis country premium forever asserts that Egypt's cost of capital never normalises, while the same models' cash flows (PHDC 25.2% escalation, TMGH deposit yield 20% flat, AMOC/ARCC kd_path easing) assume it does. Terminal share of EV is 54–74%, so every point of terminal rate is 4–6% of value. The protocol says exactly this (Standing_Research_Protocol.md 'A single flat WACC ... asserts that Egypt's cost of capital never normalises, an implausible claim'; 'WACC_TERM < WACC_EXP is a hard ASSERT'; 'Terminal ERP ... never held flat into perpetuity'; 'a WACC section without the two-anchor schedule ... is a QC FAIL') and measured it on RMDA (+162% on the DCF lens, line 493), and both PHDC's and TMGH's QC gates passed a flat rate without citing the rule.

root_causes.share_of_pessimism: PHDC: a 5-year linear glide from 26.25% to a norm-built terminal 16.26% (rf_T 12.5% + β1.049×7%, Kd_T 15%, weights as published) with g=7% moves the DCF lens 14.86 → 25.36–26.52 (my reproduction on the study's own ROWS; the range is only where year 5 lands on the path) and the weighted central 10.94 → 15.66–16.19 with the blend intact, i.e. +3 to +7% vs 15.20: this one lever closes 100–120% of the −28% gap. The published DCF's −2.2% is an accident of two errors cancelling: at the flat rate g=7% gives 10.87, and the published g=12% against a 26.25% rate is a −2 to −4% real decline. TMGH: on the study's own model with the recurring g left at the published 15%, a 10-year glide to 22.57% gives capacity 70–72, a 5-year glide 82, flat-at-terminal 102 (readers' constructions: 62–108) — i.e. 46% to 106% of the −45.8% capacity gap, and the glide SHAPE alone spans 30 points of value, which is why the r2 rule ties it to kd_path. EGCH: normalising the terminal ERP to 7% is worth only ~+0.9/sh (≈9% of the 10.22/sh gap). AMOC/ARCC: ~0% — their DCF lenses already sit at +7.4% / −2.4% of price. Rating-vs-CDS basis (chosen per study with no rule; the three most-discounted names are on the higher basis) is a second-order sub-lever: PHDC +8%, TMGH +12.5%, EGCH +0.4/sh.
root_causes.falsifier: Apply the r2 schedule exactly as written (glide fractions from each study's kd_path, terminal rf = CBE target + 5.5% real, terminal ERP normalised, Kd_T 15%) to PHDC and TMGH: if the central moves by less than 10% on either, RC-1 is not a cause there. Longer term: in a valuation-layer walk-forward (see is_the_statement_calibration_the_problem), if glide-constructed vintage fair values show larger |ln(FV_t/P_t+h)| than flat-constructed ones on held-out origins and held-out names, the glide is the wrong rule and the level is.

root_causes.cause: The four-lens blend: on every name that blends, the published discount is manufactured by two lenses that are structurally floors in a 15–25%-inflation currency — normalised earnings power capitalised at a nominal Ke of 27–37% with ZERO nominal growth (a perpetuity whose real cash flow shrinks ~13%/yr), and book value at historical cost after a ~3× devaluation put through (ROE−g)/(Ke−g) — combined with typed lens weights (0.45/0.15/0.20/0.20 etc.) that have never survived any out-of-sample test, which is the PROMOTION RULE violated by the central number itself.
root_causes.layer: VALUATION — lens specification and blend weights
root_causes.mechanism: The DCF lens is within −2.4%/+7.4% of price on AMOC, ARCC and PHDC; the weighted central is then pulled down by lenses that cannot, by construction, reach the price: E/Ke with g=0 under Ke=31% is an implied P/E of 3.2× (market pays 12.25× on the study's own FY26E EPS); the Fisher-consistent E/(Ke−π) is 1.7–2.2× larger at π=15%; justified P/B comes out 0.07× (EGCH), 0.07–0.28× (TMGH) against 1.7–4.8× paid. The constructions were transplanted from the ADNOCLS reference (UAE, Ke 9.43%, π 2%, where the wedge Ke/(Ke−π) is 1.27× and the blend landed +14.5% ABOVE price) with no inflation adaptation. AMOC's relative lens is additionally circular (own trailing multiple at 0% re-rating = price less bridge deductions, engine/amoc_study/compute.py:1609), so it can only sit below price. PHDC is also valued off the wrong class lens (cash-conversion DCF + P/E + E/Ke + raw book; no RNAV anywhere in engine/phdc_study/ against the digest's 'RE developer → SOTP/RNAV').

root_causes.layer: STATEMENT PROJECTION — specification and judgement (not the calibration machinery)
root_causes.mechanism: Nominal fades, haircuts and 'normalised' bases are applied in a currency whose own discount rate embeds 14–16% inflation, so a nominally conservative parameter is a large real decline nobody stated; and where the walk-forward produced a driver central, the study built on the pessimistic side of it (TMGH FY2026 model vs walk-forward: new sales −38.6%, development revenue −16.2%, recurring −32.7%, total revenue −23.5%, gross profit −29.4% and BELOW the record's p10 of 25,750).
